findings.title: A one-over-length issued flag key passes validation and overflows its cache slot

evidence.fact: flag_key_is_valid permits digit index20 and exits successfully when the NUL is at21. Thus f plus20 digits is accepted at21 bytes. The issued result is copied with strlen+1.
Each real flag-key cache slot is char[20+1]. The accepted21-byte name copies22 bytes into that21-byte slot.

The public model bridge permits a reply name up to127 bytes and forwards the new flag_group state. Engine model_callback uses the existing127-byte put_name path, so the C defect is reachable from a malformed public Host reply.

findings.impact: One byte beyond the identity slot is written before a refusal, potentially corrupting a neighbouring group binding. The current dialogue negative uses a22-byte name, while the positive is below the exact bound; it misses this21-byte hole.
findings.minimum_fix: Enforce the full canonical flag-key domain, including total byte length and terminating NUL, before any issued-key write. Align C with the existing Lua positive non-leading-zero digit grammar, rejecting f0/f01 as well. Keep the global127-byte name domain for other operation families unchanged. Add positive exact20-byte boundary and single-fault21-byte/long/noncanonical controls with surrounding output/cache canaries through the real exchange and public adapter; no damaged native run.

findings.title: A newly opened private group accepts a key already bound to another live group

evidence.fact: For an unbound group, FLAG_GROUP writes the returned key directly into its cache entry, without checking prior bindings.
Reply validation checks lexical key/state/count/eligibility, but does not establish fresh unique issuance before the cache commit.
open is a NEW-group operation and creates a distinct word set/key each time. Reusing an existing live key in its response is a wrong identity, not valid idempotence.

findings.impact: A faulty provider can name an existing domain-valid live key for a different newly opened C group. Both original independent words then address the same Host word, causing cross-group corruption and potentially mixing reset-eligible and reset-ineligible groups. Per-reply array/lane validation cannot detect this alias.
findings.minimum_fix: Stage the fully validated new key before committing it. Reject issuance already bound to a different private C group, preserving existing identity entries and preventing subsequent set/read under the bad binding. An identity-only uniqueness check is sufficient; add a positive two-independent-group control then one duplicate/wrong-live-key response, checking both bindings and previously held words. No public heap index, second physical store, generic epoch-transfer framework or unrelated ABI change is required.

inspected_sound_scope: The hosted mb_int getter/setter and up_update resets route to the normal campaign_entity_flag_exchange; the hosted original arrays are neither declared nor defined. No second authoritative Core bit store was found.

Core still determines the original private heap grouping/lane/reset eligibility, schedules updates, sets UPDATED after each member update and chooses every consumer call. Reset order/quarter extent, TRUE-only assertion/raw-local setter behavior, default nonmobile dispatch and raw bit31 mask are preserved at the inspected source scope. Original-profile branches retain the original flag operations.

Host request classification uses raw integer words for domain checks and validates unstated facts/identity before mutations. FlagStore methods validate array/lane/key before set/read/reset. Provider state uses try_borrow_mut and named missing/busy refusal instead of a RefCell panic. Reply echo/count/state/raw-mask/tail checks and output-after-validation are otherwise sound; they do not cure the two key-binding defects.

lifetime_and_FP_qualifications: Within one persistent SharedRoster/FlagStore binding, roster clear deliberately preserves flag words/keys, matching static-array histories. The tests support that binding scope, not arbitrary provider/store replacement or real session/heap lifetimes.

The new lifetime prose overclaims that replacement necessarily refuses every old key. New FlagStore starts its fN namespace again; a stale old key may already exist in the replacement store and name a different group. State the persistent-binding precondition and replacement limitation accurately. Do not treat fresh-store refusal or silent new-group zeroing as proof of legitimate legacy lifetime preservation. No automatic transfer/rebinding design is imposed by this review.

Test-only fresh_binding deliberately resets store plus identity cache for scenario isolation and leaves the model callback installed until that dedicated process ends. It does not prove production callback-context replacement safety.

Raw masks stay integer/bit-pattern words rather than booleans through C/Rust/Lua. New legitimate phase/array/lane casts are small exact integers, but no whole caller FPU-environment preservation, i686/x87 raw-subnormal transport or engine-C O2 result is established by these checks. Keep the declared architecture/Windows/native/FP gates honest; no new broad numerical programme or old-kernel replay is demanded.

A bad reply follows a real physical request; this source does not provide transactional rollback of arbitrary Host mutations after a callback or malformed response. The requested key fixes protect Core identity commits and existing word independence; they must not fabricate a second authoritative store to undo physical actions.
